evidenceAudit.scope: Diabetes retinal screening, urgent visual-symptom escalation and handoff to ophthalmology; treatment decisions remain specialist-led.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national retinal-screening interval document was opened.
NG242 addresses management after detection; the Saudi programme interval requires local confirmation.
SFDA status is not applicable because screening does not prescribe a medicine.

pathophysiology.summary: Chronic hyperglycaemia damages retinal microvasculature. Capillary leakage causes retinal oedema and maculopathy. Capillary closure drives retinal ischaemia and neovascularisation. Fragile new vessels can bleed or cause tractional retinal detachment.
keyMechanisms: Capillary leakage causes retinal oedema and maculopathy.
Capillary closure drives retinal ischaemia and neovascularisation.
Fragile new vessels can bleed or cause tractional retinal detachment.

symptoms: Early disease may be asymptomatic; later blurred vision, floaters, field loss or sudden visual loss may occur.
physicalSigns: Retinal microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates, macular oedema or neovascularisation on retinal imaging.
redFlags: Sudden visual loss, new shower of floaters, curtain-like field defect, painful red eye or pregnancy with known retinopathy and visual change.
precipitants: Longer diabetes duration, poor glycaemic control, hypertension, kidney disease and pregnancy.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Sudden floaters, flashes, curtain or marked visual loss needs same-day eye assessment.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Microvascular lesions, maculopathy or proliferative changes
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Grade and refer through the accredited screening/ophthalmology pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm screening status
actions: Check the date and outcome of the last accredited retinal screen and any ophthalmology follow-up.
Use the Saudi local programme interval; do not substitute a routine diabetes review for retinal imaging.

clinicalManagement.title: Triage symptoms and results
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Same day for acute visual red flags
actions: Send sudden visual loss, new floaters/curtain or painful red eye for urgent ophthalmic assessment.
Route abnormal screening grades to ophthalmology according to the local screening programme.

clinicalManagement.title: Reduce progression risk
actions: Optimise glycaemia and blood pressure without delaying ophthalmology care.
Warn that rapid, substantial HbA1c reduction can be associated with early worsening and coordinate monitoring when retinopathy is present.

medicationPlan.note: Screening does not initiate retinal medicines. Laser, intravitreal and surgical treatment belong to ophthalmology pathways.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Neovascularisation at the disc above one-quarter to one-third disc area, or elsewhere above one-half disc area with preretinal/vitreous haemorrhage, or any disc neovascularisation with such haemorrhage.

teaching.scope: Diabetes retinal screening, urgent visual-symptom escalation and handoff to ophthalmology; treatment decisions remain specialist-led.
learningObjectives: Distinguish routine screening from urgent symptomatic assessment.
Recognise proliferative and macular disease as specialist pathways.
pitfalls: Recording screening as complete without a result.
Delaying urgent eye assessment because a routine screen is booked.
keyPoints: Normal vision does not exclude early retinopathy.
Screening photography does not replace urgent examination for acute symptoms.

patientEducation: Explain that early retinopathy can be symptom-free and attendance protects sight.
lifestyleAndDiet: Support glucose, blood-pressure and smoking-risk management.
mdtReferrals: Accredited retinal screening programme, ophthalmology, diabetes team and primary care.
dischargeCriteria: Screening result documented, referral completed if abnormal and no acute visual red flags.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Use the Saudi screening programme interval and ophthalmology plan; verify attendance and outcome at the next diabetes review.
